story: Nico was halfway through the one about the lobster the size of a canoe (a smaller canoe than last time) when he and three friends gave their orders at the harbor clam shack. Nobody was listening, the cook included. Now the fryer is hot, the cook is waiting, and the order pad says only "four suppers, four drinks." Who ordered which dish, and who drank what?
clues: Whoever drank the cider ordered either the lobster roll or the fried clams.
One of Felix and the diner who ordered the crab cake drank iced tea, and the other drank lemonade.
Sam's drink was neither iced tea nor cider.
Bea's supper was either the fish tacos or the lobster roll.
The lemonade drinker had either the lobster roll or the fish tacos.
hints: Look at the crab cake in clue 2. What could its diner have drunk?
Read clue 5 next to clue 2. Both mention the lemonade. Could the crab cake's diner have had it?
No: clue 5 puts the lemonade with the lobster roll or fish tacos. So the crab cake came with iced tea, and Felix drank lemonade.

solution.key_idea: The lemonade belongs with the lobster roll or the fish tacos (clue 5), so clue 2 pairs the crab cake with iced tea.
steps: By clue 2, the crab cake's diner drank iced tea or lemonade; clue 5 rules out lemonade, so the crab cake came with iced tea.
Then Felix drank the lemonade (clue 2), and Sam, who drank neither iced tea nor cider (clue 3), had the root beer.
Clue 4 keeps Bea from the crab cake, and so from the iced tea. So Bea drank cider, and Nico had iced tea and the crab cake.
The fried clams were not Bea's (clue 4), nor lemonade-drinking Felix's (clue 5), so Sam ordered them.
Clue 1 puts the cider with the lobster roll or the fried clams, so Bea had the lobster roll, and Felix the fish tacos.
solution.epilogue: The cook got every plate to the right diner, from Nico's crab cake to Sam's fried clams. By dessert, the lobster in Nico's story had grown to the size of a fishing boat.

tip: A 'one and the other' clue always names two different people, and that is a free X.
